narrative_purpose: Shows the chapter's most believable adaptation by lining up the Earth original and the Pandoran version: a bacterium's internal chain of magnetic crystals beside the same crystal-chain seated in a Pandoran animal's sensory tissue — the magnetic sense is real, cheap, and ancient.
subject: A two-part naturalist plate joined by faint threading field lines. Left: a single translucent rod-shaped microbe with a neat internal chain of small dark cubic crystals running end to end like beads on a string, aligned along curved field lines. Right: the same kind of dark crystal chain embedded in a small pit of living tissue beneath a Pandoran animal's skin, the field lines continuing across from the left into the right.
scene: Two linked specimen studies against deep dark, the microbe enlarged at left, the skin-pit cross-section at right, both threaded by the same faint curved lines of a magnetic field.
camera: A close microscope-plate view on the left, a shallow cross-section view into skin on the right, matched in scale so the crystal chains read as the same structure.
light: Cool bioluminescent key; the crystal chains catch a faint cyan rim while staying dark and dense; the threading field lines glow very faintly in living teal; indigo shadow throughout.
palette: Void-indigo ground, Pandora cyan and living teal for the living tissue and the faint field lines, the crystals near-black with cool rims; a single faint magenta cue on the sensory nerve as a scarce accent.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, anatomical-study feel.
detail_level: Crisp on both crystal chains and the curved field lines; surrounding tissue and background softening into haze.
composition: Left and right studies bridged by the continuous field lines across a dark central gap that doubles as space for an overlaid callout.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette; the two crystal chains must read as clearly the same kind of structure at two scales — Earth microbe and Pandoran sense organ.
